mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 5% in a month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In the specified trigger regime, SPX 20-day forward returns show no correlation with the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE signal (Pearson's IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating supply-side demand, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over 30 consecutive 5-day windows, INDPRO growth does not precede SPX forward returns with a lead time < 2 days (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three months suggests deflationary pressure, which reduces expected future inflation and yields negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During the CPIAUCSL deflation regime, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains below 1.5% for four consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive 60-day forward returns due to lower financing costs and improved risk appetite.
failure_condition: In the ultra-loose regime, 60-day forward returns show no outperformance relative to a 1.5% FEDFUNDS baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in payroll employment (PAYEMS) followed by a rapid decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a labor market tightening that elevates equity risk premiums, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month and UNRATE falls by >0.3 percentage points in the following month
failure_condition: During labor-tightening episodes, SPX 20-day returns show no significant negative relationship with the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE signal (IC > -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in residential building permits (not available in the catalog) cannot be used; instead, a sustained 3-month drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests softening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 50 5-day windows, INDPRO declines do not precede SPX forward losses with a statistically significant lead time (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly rate of change of FEDFUNDS turns positive (i.e., rates are rising) while UNRATE remains above 4%, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 days due to higher real interest rates and reduced risk-taking.
failure_condition: In the specified regime, SPX 20-day returns show no significant negative relationship with the combined FEDFUNDS change/UNRATE signal (IC > -0.05).
